solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cramped hotel with some current difficulties at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ampere is a unit, an amount, of electric current
opening letter of difficulties

explanation.surface: A cramped hotel had trouble with its electricity supply at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp someone is to restrict or impede them, the same as to have hampered them.

clue.text: Cheers up, having drunk lager for free

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading the word from bottom to top
drunk suggests staggering and disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A toast is raised after someone has drunk free lager.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain cheers and ta both mean thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal at large is free, not yet captured.

clue.text: Meal was short of alcohol, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so we swap them here

blocks.note: a drink short of alcohol lacked punch

explanation.surface: A dinner was let down by weak drinks, says a famous Oxford don.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch is both a mixed drink and force; swap the L and P sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is a meal prepared at home and carried to school or work.

clue.text: In France, current ruler ultimately perfect?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, pointing to the final letter of the word

blocks.note: last letter of ruler
to hone a skill is to perfect it

explanation.surface: A French ruler in power is asked whether he is ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: Current means a river's flow, not present.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river flowing through France, and a river is a current of water.

clue.text: Refuse to go here, with stand-up being funny

indicators.note: being funny means fooling about, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone declines to perform at a comedy club with a stand-up comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is where swept-up rubbish goes before it is thrown away.

clue.text: Accountant plugs something essential to make capital

indicators.note: to plug a gap is to fill it, so the first word sits inside the second

blocks.note: a must is an essential item
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant fills a vital gap to raise funds for a business.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital means money in the surface, but here it is a capital city: Muscat is the capital of Oman.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital city of Oman, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Almost fail to catch name for butcher

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to fail to catch something is to miss it
a handle is an informal name or nickname

explanation.surface: Someone nearly fumbles a catch and calls out a name for a meat seller.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher looks like a noun but is a verb: to make a mess of.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher a task is to handle it clumsily and ruin it.

clue.text: Baseless bit of satire is to go downhill

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a skit is a short satirical sketch

explanation.surface: An unfounded satirical sketch is going to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to slide down snowy slopes, literally going downhill.

clue.text: Call for new fab dresses, showing how one may look

indicators.note: to dress something is to clothe it, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to call for is to ask
fab and ace both mean excellent
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A demand for new, fabulous dresses shows how someone might appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Dresses looks like clothes but is the verb wrapping ACE round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to glance sideways with suspicion, so askance tells how one may look.

clue.text: Want to catch ball, playing ties? Perhaps use this

definitions.text: Want to catch ball, playing ties? Perhaps use this

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are in action and moving about into a fresh order
to catch something is to hold it, so the first word holds what follows

blocks.note: to want is to lack
in football a cross is a ball played across the pitch
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: If you want to catch a ball in a game, perhaps use this.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a cross is a ball played in from the wing. Read whole, the clue also describes the stick, whose netted head catches the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacrosse stick has a netted head used to catch, carry and throw the ball, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Eco, we're told, is a 20th-century novelist

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: eco, as in eco-friendly, means environmentally green

explanation.surface: Umberto Eco seems to be described as a twentieth-century novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Eco looks like the Italian novelist Umberto Eco, but it stands for green; Graham Greene wrote Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist who wrote through the middle of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Dope engaged by factory sounding mournful

indicators.note: something engaged by another is taken up inside it, so the first word sits within the second

blocks.note: a plant is an industrial works
dope and gen both mean information

explanation.surface: Drugs are being taken at a factory, which is a sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope suggests drugs, but it means information, as does GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant sound with a sad or melancholy tone.

clue.text: Relative, endlessly strict and formidable mater?

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: a grandmother is a relative
stern and strict are synonyms

explanation.surface: A grandmother who is strict is a formidable mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Mater looks like Latin for mother, but read it as one who mates, as at chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmaster is a top-rank chess player, a formidable player who delivers checkmate.

clue.text: The setters with erudition pocketing pounds? It's merited!

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something away inside, so a letter goes into the phrase

blocks.note: the setters refer to themselves as we
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling
someone learned has erudition

explanation.surface: Learned setters pocketing money claim they have earned it.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves we; the pound sign comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-earned is fully deserved, which is what merited means.

clue.text: Warned about getting demoted and publicly flogged

indicators.note: demoted means moved lower, so that letter is taken out and put back further down

blocks.note: to warn is to caution
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone was warned about demotion and given a public whipping.
explanation.walkthrough: The C at the top of CAUTIONED moves down two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods flogged publicly are sold at auction, flog being British slang for sell.

clue.text: Assert someone partying wildly will lose face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so the first letter is lost

blocks.note: a raver is a wild party-goer

explanation.surface: Someone claims that a wild party animal will be humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or declare as true, a synonym of assert.

clue.text: Old writer not keeping any secrets

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An elderly author has decided to tell all.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer suggests an author, but it is the thing one writes with.
explanation.definitionFit: An open person is candid and frank, hiding nothing from others.

clue.text: Advice from English playmaker receiving ball

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright, a maker of plays
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A footballing playmaker in England gives advice on receiving a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: A playmaker in football sets up attacks; here it is a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a helpful hint or tip, a piece of advice.

clue.text: Bighead caught by copper around bar

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the two parts before it enclose the next word

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a lever is a rigid bar used to prise
dick is slang for a detective

explanation.surface: An arrogant person is arrested by a policeman near a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Caught and copper sit side by side and together wrap the bar. Copper is slang for police officer, and dick old slang for detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is an informal British term for a show-off who thinks they know everything, a bighead.

clue.text: Balances fizzy drink, moving head down

indicators.note: the head is the top letter, and moving it down means taking it out and reinserting it lower

blocks.note: 7 Up is a brand of lemon-lime soft drink

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink keeps someone steady as they lower their head.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up is to make equal, which is what balancing does.

clue.text: Travelling act goes round without furnishing entertainment

indicators.note: travelling means on the move, so the letters move into a new order
going round something means encircling it

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
a bare room is unfurnished

explanation.surface: A touring act performs its entertainment without any props or set.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a form of entertainment with songs and sketches at a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Intoxicated female this person's greeting

blocks.note: high means drunk or drugged
F is the abbreviation for female
this person is the setter, I, and this person's means I have, I've

explanation.surface: A drunken woman says hello in a celebratory fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for has, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A high five is a celebratory greeting in which two people slap raised palms together.

clue.text: Rating given to bachelor with timid clothing worn

indicators.note: clothing something is wrapping it up, so the word outside dresses the others

blocks.note: shy and timid are synonyms
an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A sailor and a single man share some timid, threadbare clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothing worn seems to be one phrase, but worn alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby clothes are worn out and threadbare from long use.

clue.text: Problem screening Love Island in European country there

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind a cover, so the word encloses the rest

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Trouble over screening the reality show Love Island in a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality TV dating show, but it splits into two pieces here.
explanation.definitionFit: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland, the country as named there.

clue.text: Scout in story books, small boy doing magical things

blocks.note: a tale is a story
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
S is the abbreviation for small
Harry Potter is the boy wizard

explanation.surface: A Boy Scout appears in a book series about a young wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent scout searches for promising performers or players, and so does a talent spotter.

clue.text: Throw up, with layabout appearing topless

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and topless means without it

blocks.note: a slob is a lazy, untidy person

explanation.surface: Someone vomits while a lazy person turns up shirtless.
explanation.walkthrough: Throw up suggests being sick, but it means toss high.
explanation.definitionFit: To lob is to throw something in a high arc, tossing it upward.

clue.text: Dug into strip of earth, in favour of starting

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, and starting puts it at the front
a flower bed is a strip of cultivated earth

explanation.surface: Someone digs into a strip of soil, keen to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe a matter is to investigate it deeply, the figurative sense of dug into.

clue.text: Holy place admitting use of tech's a pressing matter

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a priory is a religious house
IT, information technology, is the use of computers

explanation.surface: A religious house is urgently allowing modern technology in.
explanation.definitionFit: A priority is something that must be dealt with first, an urgent matter.
